ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a very long horizontal paper strip, the outer frame is a rectangle, and the inside is divided by three vertical lines into four adjacent rectangles from left to right. Two horizontal line segments are drawn in the figure: the first connects the centers of the 1st and 2nd rectangles, and the second connects the centers of the 3rd and 4th rectangles. Then reason: Let the widths of the four rectangles from left to right be a, b, c, d respectively. The whole paper strip is 27 cm long, so a+b+c+d=27. The distance between the centers of the adjacent 1st and 2nd rectangles is a/2+b/2; the distance between the centers of the adjacent 3rd and 4th rectangles is c/2+d/2. Therefore the sum of the lengths of the two line segments is (a/2+b/2)+(c/2+d/2)=(a+b+c+d)/2=27/2=13.5 cm.

method.method_draft: Read the picture as a long horizontal ribbon split by three vertical cuts into four adjacent rectangles in a row. The two drawn horizontal segments connect the centers of rectangle 1 to rectangle 2, and rectangle 3 to rectangle 4. From the text, take the total ribbon length as 27 cm. Let the four rectangle widths be a, b, c, d, so a+b+c+d=27. Because the centers of two adjacent rectangles lie halfway across each rectangle, the first segment has length a/2+b/2 and the second has length c/2+d/2. Their sum is (a+b+c+d)/2=27/2=13.5 cm.

The two pairs together make the entire 27 cm ribbon, so the required sum is half of 27 cm, or 13.5 cm.
